title: Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android: Take Cards on Your Phone
description: Take contactless card payments on your phone with no card machine: how Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android works in the UK, which providers offer it, and limits.
h1: Tap to Pay: take card payments on your phone
intro: Tap to Pay lets a compatible smartphone accept contactless cards and digital wallets directly, with no extra hardware. It’s ideal for occasional sales, back-up, queue-busting and getting started.

image.alt: A person holding a smartphone near a contactless payment terminal

cardText: Accept contactless on an iPhone or Android, no hardware.

sections.html:
The customer taps their contactless card, phone or watch on the back of your phone. A payment app from your provider handles the payment, so you need an account with a provider that supports Tap to Pay. On iPhone it requires an iPhone XS or later; on Android it needs a phone with NFC that meets the provider’s requirements.

In the UK, Revolut Business and NatWest’s Tyl were launch partners for Tap to Pay on iPhone, and other providers including SumUp, Square and PayPal Point of Sale have added Tap to Pay to their apps. Check each provider’s app for current support on your device.

ProsCons
No hardware to buy or carryContactless only: no chip and PIN for cards that need it
Set up in minutesNo printed receipts (digital receipts instead)
Great back-up if a terminal failsUses your phone battery and data
Usually the same rate as the provider’s readerNot ideal for busy counters

sections.h2: Contactless limits on Tap to Pay
sections.html: Card contactless limits apply in the same way as on a terminal. In March 2026 the FCA removed the fixed £100 limit, letting card issuers set their own, so limits now vary. Payments from phones and watches with Face ID, fingerprint or passcode checks weren’t subject to the £100 cap. Read the contactless limit explained.

faqs.a: Yes. Payments are encrypted and card numbers aren’t stored on your phone. The provider handles security, as with a card reader.

faqs.q: Does Tap to Pay cost more than a card reader?
faqs.a: Usually not: most providers charge their normal in-person rate. Check your provider’s pricing page.
